body: good find, this is a bug. We need to compute it on the last two dimensions.

I have two thoughts:

1. this is not a bug, but rather a limitation of the linear algebra backend. I believe ‘nuc’ uses the SVD internally, which is only implemented for 2D tensors.
2. this is a bug considering dims is not passed to the nuclear norm implementation as indicated by the traceback. We should consider erroring out for the case when dims is not None and p=‘nuc’.

body:
When `torch.norm()` is used with `dim=(2,3)` and `p='nuc'` the gradient cannot be computed because U and V  in SVD are not computed. 

Error text:
> RuntimeError: svd_backward: Setting compute_uv to false in torch.svd doesn't compute singular matrices, and hence we cannot compute backward. Please use torch.svd(compute_uv=True)


Setup:
Pytorch version: 1.3.0.dev20190914 (nightly)
OS (e.g., Linux): Ubuntu 18.04
How you installed PyTorch (conda, pip, source): conda
Python version: 3.7.4
CUDA/cuDNN version: 10.1.243 / 7.6

Code:
```
import torch

matrix1 = torch.ones(32,32)
matrix1.requires_grad = True

nuc_norm = torch.norm(matrix1, p='nuc')

nuc_norm.backward() # works fine


tensor1 = torch.ones(10,3,32,32)
tensor1.requires_grad = True

nuc_norm = torch.norm(tensor1, p='nuc', dim=(2,3))

loss = nuc_norm.sum()

loss.backward() # U, V not computed error
```

In aten/src/ATen/native/LinearAlgebra.cpp functions `nuclear_norm()` and `nuclear_norm_out()` uses `_batch_svd()` with `/*compute_uv=*/false`. Maybe this could be made optional somehow.

I changed `/*compute_uv=*/false` to `/*compute_uv=*/true` and compiled it. It seems to work on cpu but when I run it on the gpu I get:

> File "/home/canbakiskan/anaconda3/envs/torch-source/lib/python3.7/site-packages/torch/functional.py", line 694, in norm
    return torch._C._VariableFunctions.nuclear_norm(input, dim, keepdim=keepdim, out=out)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid device function
[1]    2860 segmentation fault (core dumped)  python class_deneme.py
